verdicts.quote: FIFO automatic booking is a default inferred from the outcome.

The queue is ordered by accepted joins per occurrence, including a definite order for simultaneous admissions. No priority tiers or waitlist-size product cap are assumed. … The waitlist adds no staff workflow

The same member may independently wait for distinct occurrences if allowed by existing eligibility. … whether a waitlisted member can be booked under existing payment, waiver, credit, schedule conflict and late-cancellation terms.
verdicts.missing: What happens to the other overlapping entry when the first promotion commits, including when both classes have vacancies at once.

verdicts.quote: Preserve existing cancellation rules for confirmed bookings. … No new charges, offer windows, penalties or priority schemes are introduced by this spec.
verdicts.missing: Whether existing no-show or late-cancellation penalties apply when a member misses or cancels an automatic booking they did not see.

verdicts.quote: Before cutoff, an effective booking cancellation that frees a seat triggers reevaluation by the booking authority with every member view closed.
verdicts.missing: How soon after the cancellation the authority must complete the promotion.

verdicts.quote: In-app confirmation on read is the default. … Cal sees a confirmed booking for C101. … On a failed read, show that current status is unavailable and offer retry.
verdicts.missing: The specified retry applies to reading status. There is no proactive promotion message or failure behavior for sending one.

verdicts.quote: A replayed or overlapping valid seat-release signal resolves against current occurrence state and fills only real vacancies. … A stale signal cannot reopen a closed waitlist, exceed capacity, or assign two bookings for one entry.

A new direct booking cannot claim a seat owed to a waiting entry or reserved for reconciliation. … one booking per member and occurrence. A promotion consumes its seat and ends its entry as one visible outcome.
a rule that requires fresh consent or charges at promotion, needs reconciliation with the product owner before exposing affected joins.
verdicts.missing: When a promoted booking is charged and what happens to the seat and entry if payment fails.

verdicts.quote: No priority tiers or waitlist-size product cap are assumed.
verdicts.missing: The default is uncapped. A capped waitlist would need a maximum size and a member-visible result when that size is reached.

verdicts.quote: Close enrollment and promotion at the earlier of occurrence start or an existing earlier booking cutoff, or on class cancellation. … At the exact cutoff, closure wins over a join or assignment that has yet to commit.

Other existing changes that create available seats must honor the same priority if such routes exist. … A lower capacity than current enrollment … needs reconciliation with the product owner before exposing affected joins.
verdicts.missing: How a staff capacity reduction affects existing bookings, protected vacancies and waiting entries, especially when enrollment exceeds the new capacity.

verdicts.quote: Close enrollment and promotion at the earlier of occurrence start or an existing earlier booking cutoff, or on class cancellation. End active entries without creating bookings and show closure for a class the member can still read.
The booking authority owns the durable active entry and its admission order.
verdicts.missing: Whether each entry records its join time and whether queue position is stored or calculated from admission order.

verdicts.quote: Withdrawal, ineligibility, promotion and closure remove the entry from the active queue. Retain only what is needed for the member's outcome, replay safety and established retention obligations, then remove or de-identify expired waitlist data according to the applicable policy.
verdicts.missing: The retention period or expiry rule that determines when terminal entries must be removed or de-identified.

verdicts.quote: Only the member's own protected facts reach their client. … Queue position and member lists are outside scope.
verdicts.missing: The member can see their waiting status privately. Showing their own numerical position is explicitly outside scope.

verdicts.quote: Authorized operations staff can retrieve app-owned outcomes for join, withdrawal, closure, promotion, authorization denial, assignment failure, and recovery using safe occurrence/operation correlation.
verdicts.missing: Staff have diagnostic outcomes. The spec supplies no roster view, manual promotion or removal controls, or history identifying which member was promoted at what time.

verdicts.where: Non-functional requirements, Performance, workload and recovery limits
verdicts.quote: Measure read, join and seat-to-booking latency and recovery under single-occurrence contention and independent-occurrence load.
verdicts.missing: The maximum elapsed time from an effective cancellation to a confirmed promotion.

verdicts.where: R-1.A2; Non-functional requirements, Integrity, durability and privacy
verdicts.quote: An eligible member can book through the existing path when there is a free seat and no waiting member with priority. … Existing records preserve identity and occupancy when the feature is introduced.

verdicts.where: R-1.A1; Non-functional requirements, Integrity, durability and privacy
verdicts.quote: An eligible signed-in member viewing a full, bookable class occurrence can choose **Join waitlist**. … The booking owner must inspect data and cutover compatibility before activation, including any existing queue-like state
verdicts.missing: How a class already full at activation receives its initial queue, including the treatment of any pre-existing waiting records.
